items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: Dick Hyman and a friend I met in Cleveland, a musician, had the music of those and he gave them to me and I learned to play those things. And Dick Wells do it, who I got to know, who has now died

ctx.x: You can only play it — that’s another thing about — Zezz Confrey is one that I got interested in the early days. I heard him on records and of course the hit “Song Out Of Songs.” They called that novelty piano playing in those days. And his big hit was “Kitten on the Keys.” And everybody to this day knows about that. But he also wrote things like “Coaxing the Piano,” “You Tell “em,” I heard,” “Dizzy Fingers,” “Poor Buttermilk,” let’s see what. But so many. He wrote some little novelties, things that you would…

believe came from him and called novelette, impromptu and romanza. And Dick Hyman has written and played those, and so did Dick Wells do it, who I got to know, who has now died, and Dick Hyman and a friend I met in Cleveland, a musician, had the music of those and he gave them to me and I learned to play those things. And you’d never believe that Sez Confrey could imagine those. But Confrey, his playing, we were talking about playing in different keys, if you played the piano, Confrey’s tunes could only be played…
